newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Deficom's PolCom to reduce stake in Polish Canal+.
newsitem.headline: Deficom's PolCom to reduce stake in Polish Canal+.

text.p: Deficom, a unit of Belgian holding company Definance, said on Wednesday PolCom Invest, in which it has an indirect interest, agreed in principle to cut its stake in Canal+ Polska (Poland) to 36 percent from 67 percent.
Deficom holds an indirect 49 percent of PolCom Invest.

"These agreements, which should be finalised in April 1997, allow for the entry of the Agora and Bank Handlowy groups into the capital of Telewizyjna Korporacja Partycypacyjna (TKP), the holding which controls Canal+ Polska (with the 67 percent)," Deficom said in a statement.
The Agora group is a majority shareholder of major national Polish daily Gazeta Wyborcza. Through its unit AC TV, Agora will take a 20 percent stake in TKP.
Bank Handlowy will take 11 percent in TKP via the bank's Handlowy-Inwestycje unit. This leaves PolCom Invest with 36 percent in Canal+ Polska, via TKP.
French Canal+ retains its 33 percent in Canal+ Polska.

The statement said the changes would allow Canal+ Polska to embark on future developments with the support of a stable strategic shareholdership. It said Canal+ Polska currently had over 160,000 subscribers.
